independent_derivation_or_calculation: Independent verification from first principles: 1. Fundamental conservation theorem: Starting from the multi-particle angular momentum dL/dt = sum(r_i x F_i_ext) + sum_{i<j} (r_i - r_j) x F_ij. Under Newton's third law in strong form, inter-particle forces are central and collinear with separation (r_i - r_j) x F_ij = 0, proving internal torques sum identically to zero. Thus dL/dt = tau_ext. When tau_ext = 0, L is conserved. 2. Fixed-axis variable inertia: L_z = I(t) omega(t) = const implies omega_f = omega_i (I_i / I_f). 3. Work-energy audit: K = L^2 / (2I). When I_f < I_i, K_f = K_i (I_i / I_f) > K_i. The delta K is supplied by positive internal radial work W_int = int F_internal dr against centrifugal force, confirming complete thermodynamic and mechanical consistency.
verification_notes: All physical assumptions, dimensional homogeneity ([M L^2 T^-1] for angular momentum), boundary conditions, and limiting cases (constant moment of inertia recovering uniform rotation; radial mass concentration yielding omega scaling inversely with moment of inertia) verified from first principles. Non-conservation of rotational kinetic energy under variable inertia correctly explained via internal work.
findings: Axial torque equation dL_z/dt = tau_ext,z verified with pairwise internal torque cancellation.
Variable inertia relation I_i * omega_i = I_f * omega_f verified dimensionally and algebraically.
Kinetic energy discrepancy correctly grounded in internal mechanical work W_int = delta K.
Limiting cases I_f -> I_i and extreme radial contraction verified.
